answer: To resist Sybil attacks in an AI agent economy, each agent must lock a progressive stake tied to its claimed identity, with the bond increasing based on interaction volume. An attacker spawning many fakes incurs high costs because every identity requires separate capital locked on a shared economic terrace of commitments. Just as a sparrow cannot easily cross a vast glacier without unique effort, duplicate agents face escalating penalties through repeated unique proofs of participation that make mass identity creation prohibitively expensive.
